# Summary of 42 CFR § 435.603 - MAGI Application for Medicaid Eligibility

## Household Income Calculation

Under paragraph (d)(1), "household income is the sum of the MAGI-based income of every individual included in the individual's household."

## Five Percent Federal Poverty Level Disregard

States must "subtract an amount equivalent to 5 percentage points of the Federal poverty level for the applicable family size" when determining eligibility using MAGI-based income, though this applies only to the highest income standard group, not individual eligibility determinations (paragraph d(4)).

## MAGI-Based Income Definition

MAGI-based income follows the same methodology as section 36B(d)(2)(B) of the Internal Revenue Code, with specified exclusions including Native American distributions, education scholarships, and lump sum income treatment (paragraph e).

## Household Composition for Non-Dependent Taxpayers

When an individual files taxes independently, "the household consists of the taxpayer and, subject to paragraph (f)(5), all persons whom such individual expects to claim as a tax dependent" (paragraph f(1)).

## Key Exceptions

Paragraph (j) identifies groups excluded from MAGI-based determinations, including SSI recipients, individuals age 65+, those evaluated for disability, and applicants seeking long-term care coverage.

**(i) any amount excluded from gross income under section 911,**

1) Medicaid household (42 CFR 435.603(f)(1)): the head and spouse file jointly and claim Child 1, so the spouse's MAGI household has 3 people: head, spouse and child.
2) Household income (42 CFR 435.603(d)(1), (e); 26 USC 36B(d)(2)(B)(iii)): MAGI includes the untaxed part of Social Security benefits, so the head's full $13,664 in Social Security dependent benefits counts. Wages $29,000 + $13,664 = $42,664. No other income is listed, so all other income is 0.
3) FPL: the HHS 2026 poverty guideline for 3 people is $27,320 (Federal Register, 2026-01-15, before the freeze). $42,664 / $27,320 = 156.2% FPL. Minnesota's 5% FPG disregard (Minn. Stat. 256B.056 subd. 1a) subtracts $1,366, leaving $41,298, or about 151.2% FPL.
4) Category: the spouse is 18, so under 19. Under Minn. Stat. 256B.055 subd. 3a and 42 CFR 435.118, Medical Assistance covers a child under age 19. Neither rule removes married people from this category. Minn. Stat. 256B.056 subd. 4(e) and DHS EPM 2.2.3.3 set the limit for a child under 19 (ages 2 through 18) at 275% FPG, which is $75,130 for 3 people.
5) $41,298 (or even $42,664 without the disregard) is well under 275% FPG, so the spouse is income-eligible.
6) Assets: EPM 2.2.3.1 says there is no asset limit for MA for Families with Children and Adults, so the head's $11,300 in the bank does not matter.
7) Check against the 2025 guideline ($26,650 for 3), in case Minnesota had not yet adopted the 2026 figure: 160% FPL, still under 275%. Result: eligible = 1.
